papers.title: Boundary phenomena for slow recurrences:finite and infinite critical sets
papers.abstract: For a second-order recurrence with positive integral coefficients, the slow length of an integer is the largest index at which it can occur when the initial terms range over positive integers. Spiro conjectured that, among a finite set of relatively prime recurrence pairs, a pair is slowest infinitely often precisely when its growth constant is strictly less than the square of the smallest growth constant. We study the equality case. For $T_m=\{(m-1,m),(m^2-1,m^2)\}$, the larger-growth pair attains the maximal slow length, with ties allowed, on $\Theta_m(\log x)$ integers up to $x$ whenever $m\ge3$, whereas for $m=2$ its complete set of slowest integers is $\{1,2,25\}$. We give certificates for the infinite examples and prove a bounded-seed theorem that limits the possible initial pairs at each critical index.

papers.title: Construction, Enumeration and Duality of Perfectly Balanced Musical Sets of Order $2pq$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a comprehensive study of perfectly balanced musical sets, also known in the literature as vanishing sums of roots of unity, in the particular case of order $2pq$. Starting from the well-established result concerning the decomposition of such sets as an integer linear combination of regular polygons, we first provide an algebraic formalization that allows to explicitly construct all these sets. We then propose six different decompositions of each set into regular polygons. Moreover, by investigating their combinatorial enumeration, we derive a formula for the exact number of these sets for a given order $2pq$, and describe their distribution and cardinality for the particular case of order $6p$. One of the main results concerns the duality that can be established between these sets. In particular, we prove that every non-periodic minimal perfectly balanced set of order $2pq$ can be combined with another one to produce a self-complementary $2p$-periodic set, and the reciprocal also holds. Finally, we demonstrate that the modulus of the discrete Fourier transform coefficients of dual sets are related. All these results shed new light on the distribution of perfectly balanced sets of order $2pq$ and suggest new mathematical questions in a more general case.

papers.title: Irreducibility of the Cuboid Polynomial $P_{a,u}(t)$ via a Rank-Zero Elliptic Curve
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the even monic degree-8 cuboid polynomial $P_{a,u}(t)$ introduced by R. A. Sharipov in the first-cuboid specialization of his cuboid equations. For nonzero integers $a,u$ with $u^2\neq a^2$ we prove that $P_{a,u}(t)$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[t]$ (equivalently, in $\mathbb{Q}[t]$), thus confirming Sharipov's irreducibility conjecture in this two-parameter case. Over $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)$ we have a factorization $P_{a,u}(t)=H_-(t)H_+(t)$ into two conjugate quartics. We show that reducibility of either $H_\pm$ would force the discriminant of a certain quadratic in $S=t^2$ to be a square in $K$, which in turn implies (via $\tau=(au/\Delta)^2$, where $\Delta=u^2-a^2$) the existence of a rational point $(y,v)\in\mathcal{C}(\mathbb{Q})$ on the genus-one quartic $\mathcal{C}: v^2=16y^4+136y^2+1$ with $y^2=\tau$. We give an explicit isomorphism $\overline{\mathcal{C}}\simeq E$ with the elliptic curve $E: Y^2=X(X-8)(X-9)$, which has conductor $48$ and Mordell-Weil rank $0$. Enumerating $E(\mathbb{Q})$ and tracing back to $\mathcal{C}(\mathbb{Q})$ rules out the only possible values $\tau\in\{0,1/4\}$, and hence excludes any further factorization of $H_\pm$ in $K[t]$. A quadratic Galois descent then yields the irreducibility of $P_{a,u}(t)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{Z}$.

papers.title: Irreducibility of the Cuboid Polynomial $Q_{p,q}(t)$ via the Rank-One Chabauty-Coleman Method
papers.abstract: Let $Q_{p,q}(t)\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be Sharipov's even monic degree-$10$ second cuboid polynomial, with coprime positive integers $p\ne q$. We prove that $Q_{p,q}(t)$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$, and hence over $\mathbb{Z}$. More generally, the normalized associated quintic $P_s(x)$ and its composition $P_s(t^2)$ are irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ for every $s\in\mathbb{Q}\setminus\{0,\pm1\}$. The proof reduces linear and quadratic factors to rational points and horizontal conjugate pairs on one fixed genus-$2$ curve. A certified rank upper bound for its Jacobian, together with an exact divisor calculation, gives a rank-one annihilating differential at the prime $3$. For the quadratic-factor case, the symmetric coordinates of a horizontal pair lie on an explicit double cover of an elliptic quartic. All rational affine points on this model are $3$-adically integral and reduce to six smooth residue classes. The pulled-back differential is a unit in each class, proving that six displayed points form the complete list. Their coordinates exclude every admissible parameter. A negative real root of the irreducible quintic then supplies the additional degree argument required for irreducibility of the degree-$10$ polynomial. The rank computation and all exact arithmetic certificates are specified explicitly for reproduction.
